situation: Had a final-round interview yesterday for a product designer role at Loop Health with the head of design, Marcus. He talked a lot about their accessibility audit. I fumbled a question about design systems.
reply:
Hi Marcus,
Thank you for the conversation yesterday. Your point about the accessibility audit changing how the team prioritises the backlog stuck with me; it's the kind of work I'd want to be part of. One thing I'd add to my answer on design systems: at Fenwick I set up the shared component library in Figma that cut our handoff time roughly in half, which I didn't explain well in the moment. I'm very interested in the role and happy to send anything else that helps.
Best,
Alina
note: Within 24 hours, one specific thing he said, one clarification, one line of interest. Not a second cover letter.

situation: 今天下午和合作方开了项目启动会，定了几件事：先做华东区试点，对方的孙经理负责提供门店数据，我负责出排期。想发个会后纪要。
reply:
各位好，感谢今天的时间，简单整理一下会议结论，确保大家理解一致：
- 先做华东区试点，覆盖上海和杭州共12家门店。
- 孙经理：10月9日前提供门店销售数据。
- 我：10月10日前发出完整排期。
- 待定：试点期间是否需要法务审核活动规则，由赵律师10月8日前确认。
如有记错的地方请直接指出。
陈静
note: 会后纪要当天发，每一项都有负责人和日期，写下你希望成为事实的版本。

situation: Interviewed for an account manager job at a logistics company 3 weeks ago, the recruiter Hannah said I'd hear back by last Friday. Nothing. I already sent one check-in 10 days ago.
reply: Hi Hannah, I'll take the quiet as the timing not working out on your side. Thanks again for a well-run process, and I'd be glad to hear from you if a similar role opens up at Crestline.
note: One check-in was already sent, so this is the short closing note. It leaves a good last impression without chasing.
